items.title: Rent tax breaks due from December 1
items.body: Published Royal Decree-law 29/2026 is due to apply from December 1, but parliamentary validation is pending. Landlords cutting rent by more than 5% could get up to a 100% IRPF (personal income tax) reduction on net rental income, subject to conditions. Eligible tenants could request one- or two-year extensions.

items.title: Regulated electricity prices climb 62.2% over year
items.body: Regulated electricity prices averaged 0,2198 euros/kWh in November's first 11 days, up 62.2% from a year earlier. Selectra estimates that running common household appliances for an hour costs 61.5% more than a year ago. Experts advise using appliances during cheaper hours, normally 12:00 to 16:00.

items.title: Hernández de Cos leads ECB succession race
items.body: Bank for International Settlements managing director and former Banco de España governor Pablo Hernández de Cos is favoured to become ECB president. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on November 13 that a deal is days away, but talks have not ended. The other official candidate is Dutchman Klaas Knot.

items.title: RTVE schedules election showdown for November 19
items.body: RTVE will broadcast a debate between Prime Minister and PSOE candidate Pedro Sánchez and PP candidate Alberto Núñez Feijóo on November 19 at 22:00. An eight-party debate follows on November 23. Both precede the November 29 general elections.

items.title: Government approves challenge to Valencia aid rules
items.body: The cabinet approved a Constitutional Court challenge to Valencia's residency-based social aid rules on November 10. The Council of State had unanimously found sufficient legal grounds on November 5. The case could shape access to benefits and wider plans for Vox's "national priority" policy.

items.title: Canary Islands record 1,488 migrant rescues in one day
items.body: Maritime rescue crews and the Guardia Civil rescued 1,488 people from 14 boats on November 14, a provisional record for the Canary route. The previous high was 1,461 in 2020. El Hierro received 1,235 people. Eighteen people who landed in Gran Canaria and Tenerife needed hospital care.

items.title: Spanish chemist ranks 35th worldwide for influence
items.body: Chemist Avelino Corma ranks first in Spain and 35th worldwide in Stanford University's World's Top 2% Scientists ranking. The Universitat Politècnica de València researcher is urging the next government and private companies to invest more in science and bring back talent trained abroad.

items.title: Pension levy planned to reach 1% in January
items.body: From January 2027, the MEI (Intergenerational Equity Mechanism) pension contribution would rise from 0.90% to 1% of the contribution base, says Social Security civil servant Alfonso Muñoz. Workers would pay 0.17% and companies 0.83%. The levy helps fund higher pension spending as the baby boom generation retires.

items.title: Banks offer deposits above 3% for years
items.body: Banks are extending fixed-rate deposits to retain customers and secure cheap funding. Four-year offers include Klarna at 3.24% and EBN at 3.1%, while Bank di Mare offers 3.4% for two years. Savers can lock in returns but could miss higher rates if the ECB raises them.

items.title: Cabinet approves broader special status for large families
items.body: The cabinet approved a decree-law to move four-child families into the special large-family category automatically. Some three-child families would also move, such as those with two children from the same birth. Three-child families qualifying by income must apply and show income per member of at most 150% of the IPREM benchmark.

items.title: November 19 postal vote deadline for returning Spaniards
items.body: Spaniards registered as overseas voters who are temporarily in Spain must request a postal vote by November 19 and send voting documents before November 25. Those voting abroad can use consular post or vote in person for the November 29 election. They no longer need to request voting papers.

items.title: Madrid families seek talks after month-long teacher strike
items.body: Madrid families' groups are pressing regional Education Minister Mercedes Zarzalejo to negotiate after a month of teacher strikes. They have asked the ombudsman to examine whether pupils' right to education is protected. Striking teachers plan a court challenge to minimum-service rules.

items.title: Spain face England with group lead at stake
items.body: Spain and England meet with the group lead at stake in the national team's final match of the year. Spain top the FIFA rankings, while England sit fourth. Spain coach Luis de la Fuente calls it one of the best matches in world football.
